# Engineering Onboarding Guide

**Owner:** Nadia Okafor · **Status:** Living doc. First used for Sarah Kim (started 2026-07-07); revised after Theo Brandt's first week (started 2026-08-18) and again 2026-09-21.

Welcome. Stencil moves real people's money, so the first few weeks are about learning how things work and why they're built this way, then shipping something small to production in your first week.

## Before day one

Your manager or onboarding buddy makes sure of the following:

- Laptop arrives pre-enrolled in MDM (MDM Rollout Plan). Don't skip the enrollment restart; you won't get SSO without it.
- SSO account and a hardware security key are waiting for you.
- You have a named onboarding buddy from your pod, not your manager.
- Calendar invites for week one are already sent.

## Week one

| Day | What |
|---|---|
| 1 | Laptop, SSO, hardware key, GitHub. Meet your buddy. Read this page and Engineering Culture - Operating Principles. |
| 2 | Local environment for the monolith (target: tests running by lunch). Walk through Architecture Overview 2026 with your buddy. |
| 3 | Pick a starter ticket (labelled `good-first-pr`). Read Code Review Standards. |
| 4 | First PR open. Security training. Sit in on the TL sync as an observer. |
| 5 | First PR merged and deployed. Write down three things that confused you and send them to Nadia. |

Sarah merged on day 4. Theo merged on day 5. Both counted.

## Required reading (first two weeks)

Read in this order. Each is short.

1. Engineering Culture - Operating Principles
2. Code Review Standards
3. On-Call Rotation Design and Incident Review Process
4. Postmortem - April 6 ACH Pipeline Failure (why money movement is held to a different bar)
5. ADR-024 - Move ACH Processing Off Sidekiq
6. Feature Flag Policy
7. Information Security Policy

Payments engineers also read: ACH Pipeline - Design Doc, Pillar Bank Integration Notes, Round-up Sweep Job - Overview.

Mobile engineers also read: ADR-028 - iOS App Rewrite vs. Incremental and the TCA notes in the iOS repo README.

## Access you'll get, and when

| Access | When | Who approves |
|---|---|---|
| GitHub, Linear, Slack, Datadog (read) | Day 1 | Automatic |
| Non-production AWS | Week 1 | Pod TL |
| Production read (logs, dashboards) | Week 2 | Pod TL |
| On-call shadow | After 30 days | Pod TL |
| Production database, partner portals | Only if your role needs it | TL and Sam Whitfield; reviewed quarterly (Access Review Procedure) |

Don't ask a teammate to share their access. Ask for your own.

## 30 / 60 / 90

- **30 days:** shipped several small changes; can explain how a deposit moves from the app to Pillar Bank; shadowed one on-call week.
- **60 days:** owned a small feature end to end; reviewed others' PRs; first on-call week as secondary.
- **90 days:** you're a regular contributor. First check-in against the Performance Review Framework with your manager.

## What we changed after Theo's first week

- iOS simulator setup took most of day 2. The script now installs the right Xcode components; target is under 2 hours.
- Theo didn't know who to ask about design questions. Lin Zhao now does a 30-minute design walkthrough in week one for every mobile hire.
- Reading list was too long. Cut it to the seven above.

## For buddies

- Daily 15-minute check-in for the first two weeks.
- Review their first three PRs yourself.
- Tell their manager early if they're stuck. Being stuck in week one is normal; staying stuck is a process failure, not theirs.

Open question: should new Payments engineers get a standing slot at the Pillar ops sync in their first month? Sarah found it useful. Marcus Bell thinks it's too early.
